messages:
carmen: Heads-up from the nightly perf run — prefills and decodes are still contending in the same kernel lanes and we're seeing a ~12% p99 tail increase vs last week's baseline. Flamegraph attached (s3://redwood-perf/prefill-decode/6325/flame.svg).

carmen: Quick log snippet:
```
[2026-03-20T02:14:05Z] req=0x7fa kv_cache_miss prefill len=128 tokens=64 batch_sz=6 kernel=matmul_v2
[2026-03-20T02:14:05Z] req=0x7fa handshake split prefill->decode queue_shrink:8->4 token_budget=40
[2026-03-20T02:14:05Z] req=0x7fa kernel_switch decode->prefill due_to_affinity=false latency_ms=2.3
```

carmen: Observations: lots of micro-switches between kernels when small prefills land while decodes are draining. KV priming latency also spikes when prefill batches evict small decode KV lines. @raj can you grab a trace for the 6325 run? :eyes: 

raj: grabbing traces now. will post a bundled trace + perf counters. my first thought: we need an explicit phase-window smoother to avoid immediate kernel handoffs on small queue events.

liam: agree. also think the current token_budget target (40) is too aggressive for mixed traffic. propose token-weighted batch gating: compute effective_budget = min(global_token_budget, avg_tokens_in_queue * 1.5) and prefer forming prefill batches only if their effective_budget > threshold. that reduces micro-batching churn.

evie: wanted to try a simpler scheduler tweak first: add 20ms hysteresis on kernel affinity so once a lane picks prefill kernels it sticks for 20ms unless overloaded. small change, low risk. we can AB against canary.

carmen: Both ideas sound promising. Liam's token-weighted gating would reduce wasted kernel switches; Evie's hysteresis addresses noise. Let's prototype both behind flags. I sketched configs: 

```
# experiment: token_weighted_gating_v1
batcher.token_budget.global=40
batcher.token_budget.gating_mode=weighted
batcher.token_budget.weight_factor=1.5
batcher.token_budget.min_threshold=32

# experiment: kernel_affinity_hysteresis_v1
scheduler.affinity.hysteresis_ms=20
scheduler.affinity.strict=false
```

carmen: Also found KV priming issue: small prefill batches cause eviction of recently-used decode KV shards. Suggest adding a kv_reserve_pool for decode hot-shards (reserve 1-2 shards per active decode flow) and a soft-eviction policy.

raj: trace + perf counters posted: s3://redwood-perf/traces/6325/trace.tar.gz. notable counters: kernel_switch_rate=0.87/s, kv_eviction_rate=0.12/s, prefill_batch_sz_median=3. prefer to try hysteresis first and measure kernel_switch_rate delta.

liam: if we enable token gating, we should also tweak batch formation loop to prefer coalescing small prefills into an opportunistic batch for up to 10ms when decode lane is quiet. call it "opportunistic_prefill_window_ms=10".

evie: testing plan: 
- canary A: hysteresis_ms=20 only (1% traffic)
- canary B: hysteresis_ms=20 + opportunistic_prefill_window_ms=10 (1% traffic)
- canary C: token_weighted_gating enabled (1% traffic)
collect: p50/p95/p99 latency, kernel_switch_rate, kv_eviction_rate, tail error spikes. run for 4 hours.

perf-bot: nightly-check: run 6325 -> baseline compare ready. p99 increased 12.3% baseline->current, kernel_switch_rate +22%, kv_eviction_rate +9%. See /perf/6325/summary.

carmen: thanks — I'll open 3 experiment PRs and wire flags. can we get infra to roll canaries tomorrow 02:00 UTC? @raj assign infra runbook.

raj: assigned, infra run tomorrow slot confirmed. I will also add an extra KV metric: 'kv_reserve_hits' to see reserve pool effectiveness.

liam: one more thought — kernel selection hysteresis should be tied to recent batch composition, not just wall clock. maybe use a small EWMA on prefill_ratio and block switches until EWMA < 0.3. but that's v2.

evie: noted. for now keep the changes minimal and observable.

carmen: perfect. will push PRs and post links here once ready. thanks team :rocket:
